# Which modes dominate the literature? A study design {.unnumbered}

[Drafted]{.status .drafted} [a design, not a result · the group decides in meeting 1 whether to run it · full text in the private repository]{.status-line}

## Questions

1. What share of papers in a field presents each mode as its decisive move, and how has that changed since 1970?
2. Among field-shaping papers, is the distribution of modes different from the field's baseline?
3. How does mode relate to impact, novelty, interdisciplinarity, and depth, holding year and subfield fixed?
4. Where a trajectory is documented, does the presented mode match the reconstructed one?

- Question 4 needs notebooks, retrospectives, and people in the room; the literature cannot answer it

## What is already measured

- Research strategies in biomedicine: mostly conservative, innovation rare and rewarded more [@foster2015]
- Atypical combinations plus a conventional core predict impact [@uzzi2013]
- Interdisciplinarity: less output, more citations [@leahey2017]
- Disruption declines across the literature [@park2023; @wu2019]; the measure inflates with reference lists [@petersen2025]
- Large fields entrench their canon [@chu2021]
- Not measured: the share of modes of inquiry in a literature, coded against a stated taxonomy
  - Nearest: hypothesis-driven vs data-driven biology argued from cases [@kell2004; @glass2008]; what ecologists count as good science [@elliott2016]
- Step 0: a proper search for prior work of this kind, in [Novelty Dossier](rubrics.qmd#novelty-dossier-v1) form

## Corpus

- Unit: the paper. Source: OpenAlex (abstracts where allowed, references, citations, topics, field-normalized citation percentile)
- Home corpus: seismology, so the group can judge the coding
  - Feasibility, September 6, 2026: about 22,000 articles 1970 to 2020 under the seismology topic; about 10,000 with an abstract; about 290 cited more than 100 times
  - Define the corpus by journal set, not topic label (BSSA, JGR Solid Earth, GJI, SRL, seismology papers in GRL and Nature Geoscience)
- Comparison corpus: molecular biology, the field Platt held up as fast
- Abstracts for a first pass; the pilot codes full text

## Coding scheme

- Decisive mode (one of the ten in the [glossary](glossary.qmd)); sub-mode; secondary modes
- Hypothesis stated before the result, as presented: yes / no / cannot tell
- Intervention on the system: yes / no
- New instrument or method as the contribution: yes / no
- New data: collected / reused / none
- Shared infrastructure: yes / no
- Coder confidence, three levels, one sentence
- Coders see title, abstract, full text; not journal, authors, year, or citations [@kapoor2023]

## Procedure

- **Pilot**: 100 random papers; two coders; agreement per variable; every disagreement recorded; glossary revised where a definition fails
- **Classifier**: a language model with the revised glossary as instructions; 300 human-coded held-out papers; precision and recall per mode, and the confusion between modes; treated as a measurement instrument [@flake2020]; re-checked after every glossary change
- **Scale**: the full corpus; low-confidence papers sampled for human review

## Measures

- **Impact**: field-and-year-normalized citation percentile [@radicchi2008; @waltman2016]; top 1% and 10% strata; citations are attention as well as use [@bornmann2008]; add data reuse and method adoption where possible
- **Field-shaping**, three ways, reported separately: disruption index [@funk2017; @wu2019] with the inflation correction [@petersen2025]; canonical status [@chu2021]; sleeping beauties [@ke2015]
- **Novelty**: atypical journal pairs [@uzzi2013]; word-embedding distance [@shibayama2021]; known problems recorded [@fontana2020]
- **Interdisciplinarity**: diversity of cited fields (variety, balance, disparity) [@stirling2007; @porter2009; @wagner2011]
- **Depth**: reference concentration for the paper; topic concentration for the first author [@teodoridis2018]

## Analysis plan, frozen before coding

- Mode shares by decade, with confidence intervals (question 1)
- Mode shares in each field-shaping stratum vs a matched random sample; three strata separately (question 2)
- Impact percentile on mode, with year and subfield controls and the other measures as covariates; the same with "hypothesis stated" in place of mode (question 3; the direct test of the seminar's thesis at the level of narrative)
- The seminar's thirty reconstructed episodes: presented vs reconstructed mode, against impact (question 4)
- Everything else labelled exploratory [@tukey1962]

## What can go wrong

- The paper reports the presented mode, not the trajectory; abstracts follow templates; funders have wanted hypotheses since @platt1964
- Only published work is visible; failed modes are not
- Mode is not quality; the regression controls for what can be measured
- The classifier learns the field's conventions; human coding on a held-out set is the only check
- "Field-shaping" is three constructs, not one

- The frozen analysis plan with its date
- The classifier's validation report
- A short paper
- The coded corpus doubles as training and evaluation data for the mode-aware reader in the [design notes](agent-design.qmd)
